newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sees '96 sugar output at 280,000 Tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Romania sees '96 sugar output at 280,000 Tonnes.

text.p: Romania's 1996 sugar output is expected to total 280,000 tonnes but production will not be enough to cover domestic demand, raising prospects of imports of 120,000 tonnes of raw sugar, an official said on Thursday.
"The import of the 120,000 tonnes will be exempt from customs duties and carried out without government guarantees," Agriculture Minister Alexandru Lapusan told a news conference.
The ministry expects a crop of around 2.7 million tonnes of sugar beets. Romania's 1995 sugar output was 300,000 tonnes.
Only 22 out of 30 refineries would be operational in 1996, Lapusan said. The ministry, he said, had taken steps to ensure smooth harvesting and proper storage for this year's crop.
Lapusan said his ministry was considering the use of excess capacities at refineries to process beets from neighbouring Hungary, Moldova and Yugoslavia.

A source in the sugar sector told Reuters recently that beets on 23,000 hectares of the 161,950 sown had been lost due to a harsh winter and late snows. Lack of proper machinery, inadequate storage and transport delays added to the problems.
An acute shortage of fuel which hit the farming sector recently might also affect sugar beet harvesting, a ministry source also said.
Beet output has been in continuous decline in recent years, reflecting poor management of crop lands and a lack of funds.

Lapusan said private farmers had been discouraged by the repeated failure of the state-run refineries to pay for crops in time and had consequently switched to other crops, drastically diminishing the areas put under sugar beet.
Lack of funds had also forced farmers to use only 100 kg of fertiliser per ha this year, against a recommended 160 kg.
Data show the country imported 246,489 tonnes of sugar last year and 90,230 during January-May 1996. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom +401 312-0264
